sermon.title: Adding
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In “Adding,” a Vine Cluster guest speaker (who refers to Mr. Kincer in the third person) walks through 2 Peter 1:5-10 and says believers must add virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and agape love to their faith so they will not be barren. He contrasts Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego—who kept adding and were found ten times better—with Solomon, who received great wisdom but threw out virtue and fell. He closes with the promise that if you add to your faith you will never fall and will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Guest speaker: he refers to “Mr. [unclear]” and later “Mr. Kincer,” so this is not Pastor Kincer preaching. Caption fixes kept as spoken intent: “agy”→agape, “unix”→eunuchs, “mhach/abedo”→Meshach/Abednego, “breath of understanding”→breadth (1 Kings 4:29), “wife lives”→wives. He paraphrases John 14 as “These things in My house are many mansions” (kept as spoken). He says “Daniel 1 through 2” in the captions (rendered “1 through 12” as the book length he is pointing to—flag for Michael). Abortion, sex outside marriage and drugs are named as sins he says moral excellence rejects; kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What does “add to your faith” mean in 2 Peter 1:5?
chunks.short_answer: He says the term implies you can’t stay in one place: as soon as you hear it you say you’ve got to do more than just believe or accept Christ in your heart—you’ve got to move on. The first addition is virtue, moral excellence.
chunks.text: We’re going to step back and take a broad view and look at it. We’re going to go to that verse in Second Peter 1:5, and now you guys know it by heart. And you have all these things. And the term “add to your faith,” it implies that you can’t stay in one’s place. It’s such a good word. As soon as you hear it, you say, “I’ve got to do more than just believe. I’ve got to do more than just accept Christ in my heart. I’ve got to move on.” And it’s so good. And we’re going to look at this scripture and how much God is going to do for us. So “add to your faith virtue.” The virtue it’s talking about there is the moral excellence. As we learned, you’re committed to, you know, when you come to Christ.

chunks.section_question: What is virtue or moral excellence in this sermon?
chunks.short_answer: He says moral excellence means saying no to sin: you don’t abort babies, you don’t have sex outside of marriage, you throw the drugs out. Just by saying no and living that way, he says God begins to bless you before you even add the other things.
chunks.text: You have to say no to sin. The moral excellence: you don’t abort babies anymore, you’re not going out and have sex outside of marriage, you throw the drugs out, you say no to that stuff. And just by saying no to that, just by living a moral excellent life, it will bless you. Just by saying no, you haven’t even added these other things, but by getting rid of the sin and let God do a work in your life, it begins to bless you. And that’s just the first step. And then he says to add knowledge. And as we teach here, you’ve got to read the Scriptures when you go home. It’s not just Sunday morning. Mr. [unclear] can’t come up in 15 minutes and fill you with enough bread to last a week. Amen. We’ve got to read, we’ve got to study the Scriptures, we’ve got to know for ourselves.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about self-control and patience?

chunks.text: Self-control: you know, it’s also like the moral excellence, you have to say no, but self-control is also self-controlling your mind, taking care of it first in your mind, stopping that. The tongue: the Bible says the tongue is an unruly evil. Controlling the tongue—oh, man. Living in this life, getting married, having kids, you just have to learn. It’s a crash course in tongue control, right? Amen. You live with somebody, everything’s changing and you don’t know what’s going on. And patience—patience, my God, I need patience. Just like I was saying, you get married, you have kids, or just being a teenager having patience with your parents. Man, I’m telling you, that’s right. They can be tough. It can seem tough being a child. As parents, a husband and wives—patience. Man, you know, you’ve said these things over and over. You’ve got to have patience. Or maybe you don’t get it and you’ve got to have patience with yourself.

chunks.section_question: What kind of love does he say we must add?
chunks.short_answer: He points to agape love as defined in 1 Corinthians 13, not the world’s love. He says Jesus had so much love for the Pharisees that He came into conflict with them, because real love tells people when they are wrong.
chunks.text: Like godliness—Christlike. Brotherly kindness: we come in here this morning, there are so many people loving one another, being kind sincerely. It was good. It was such a good feeling this morning in this place. And agape love, as defined in 1 Corinthians 13—you guys know that scripture. We all know about love, and it’s not love that’s defined by the world. It’s a different kind of love. It’s a love Jesus had. So much love for the Pharisees that he came in conflict with them. He rocked their world. He approached them and he said, “No, you’re wrong,” why? Because he loved them. And people don’t see love that way. They feel like it’s only a fuzzy. God is going to conflict with you. He’s going to approach you. Why? Because he loves you and he knows what’s best for you. He’s the Creator. Somewhere we’ve got to come to the realization that God really is the Creator. God really has so much power we don’t even understand it. And we sit here and we say to God, “What do you know, God?” What? He knows everything.

And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. chunks.section_question: What does 2 Peter 1:8 say if these things abound?
chunks.short_answer: After Mr. Kincer has gone through the list, he reads that if these additions abound you will be neither barren nor unfruitful. He compares barrenness to Death Valley and says God wants us flourishing and bearing fruit.
chunks.text: But it goes on to say—we want to look at these. You know, we talked a lot about these things, and Mr. Kincer has gone through. But after this, after the verse in 2 Peter 1:8, it’s very important what it says afterwards. It says, “For if these things”—talking about the additions to faith—“if these things abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful.” Barren: useless. You know, a desert is just—you go out there, it’s cracked. Death Valley. You can ride on it, you can tear it up, but that’s about it, you know. And it’s okay to be in a desert, but God wants us to be flourishing. God wants us to bear fruit. And yes, we do go through times of no water, and it causes us to dig deep. But when we apply these things, when these things abound in us, when we are exercising, when we take the knowledge and we go to the Scriptures and we get knowledge, we go to high school and we’re actually paying attention, and we go to college because we’re trying to add knowledge to ourselves—you know, God is going to bless those things. When we are more adding virtue, saying no. Amen.

chunks.section_question: How does bearing fruit help other people?
chunks.short_answer: He says when you bear fruit you have something to give out, like an orchard whose oranges go throughout California and nourish people. Christ wants to transform who we are and people around us.
chunks.text: When we add self-control, when we are trying to add patience, God is going to honor that. And it says right here, if these things abound you will neither be barren nor unfruitful—that means you’re going to be fruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. And you see, the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ—Christ wants to transform who we are, and not just us but people around us. You see, when you bear fruit you have something to give out. You have a tree, an orchard. It gets sent out throughout all of California, and people partake of that, and they get nourishment and vitamin C from oranges and all this stuff. Amen. Because somebody took the time to plant, somebody took the time to water, somebody took the time to take care and add to that seed.

chunks.section_question: What happens if someone lacks these qualities?
chunks.short_answer: From 2 Peter 1:9 he says whoever lacks them is blind and shortsighted, like the Pharisees who believed in God and learned Scriptures but didn’t add Christ and forgot they were cleansed from old sins. Sin will creep in and hurt you.
chunks.text: Second Peter 1 verse 9. You know, God is so—he’s like, you know, you’re going to be so—if these things abound in you, you’re going to be blessed, you’re going to be fruitful. And on the other side, if you don’t, it’s rough. You know, in the Old Testament, if you listen to Me, you’re going to be blessed. You’re going to be—oh man—you’re going to be great throughout the earth. If you don’t, you’re going to have a big problem. You’re not going to have blessing. You’re going to have problems in your life. Line: Second Peter 1:9. And those here that are young, and you’ll find as you grow up, if we don’t add these things, you’re going to find that sin is going to creep in. Sin is going to hurt you. “Whoever lacks these things”—these qualities—“is blind, shortsighted, seeing only what is near to him.” Blind, just like the Pharisees. The Pharisees, they weren’t adding to their faith. They believed in Abraham, they believed in God, but they didn’t add anything. They were adding knowledge, they were learning the Scriptures, but they missed it. They were blind. They couldn’t see. They weren’t adding Christ. “And has forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins.” Again, here we see adding to our faith. We come out of sin. We’re cleansed from sin. Christ died on the cross to cleanse us, to get rid of that, to make us a new creature. It’s plain in the Scriptures, the process that we need to go through.

chunks.short_answer: He says if you do these things—if you add to your faith—you will never fall, and you will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom. He wants that rich welcome, and says Jesus spoke of valuable mansions for His people.
chunks.text: Amen. And such a powerful promise in 2 Peter 1:10. It goes on to say, if you do these things—if you add to your faith—you will never fall. And that is a promise worth seeking after. That is such a powerful promise. It says, and you will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom. There’s different kind of welcomes. There’s a rich welcome and a poor welcome. And “oh yeah, yeah, you believe, come on in,” and “oh, there he is, the guy who added to his faith, the guy who did—come on in.” Man, you know, I don’t know what that means, a rich welcome, but I want a rich welcome. You know, Jesus keeps saying, “These things in My house are many mansions.” You know, he’s got something for us, and he’s saying mansions to let us know they’re valuable. chunks.section_question: How did Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego add to their faith?
chunks.short_answer: From Daniel 1:4 he says they were already adding knowledge and wisdom as young men with no blemish, skillful and teachable. He urges young people to stand out, believe in God and add to their faith the way he did in school.
chunks.text: Daniel 1:4. It says that the servant, the prince of the eunuchs, was to go out and find men, children of Israel, with no blemish, well-favored, skillful in wisdom and cunning in knowledge and understanding science, and teachable. Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego—I always say the name because I can’t remember their original names—they were already working on adding to their faith. They believed. They believed in God, and they were adding knowledge, they were adding wisdom. See, these young men stood out. And you guys, as young people, we’ve got to decide as young people to be individuals, to stand out. Cry, believe in God, stand and add to your faith. It’s going to have the best effect in your life. As a young person in high school I was different, and people around me were different. When I went to college I was different. When I was in college I actually listened. When I was in high school I listened. I did my work. And I tell you, that has blessed me ever since I’ve been out of college. And it’s going to hurt you if you don’t. If you don’t add.

chunks.section_question: How did God add to Daniel’s knowledge?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Daniel 1:17 and 1:20: they had a level of knowledge, then God gave them more, and the king found them ten times better. Their greatest ability was submitting to adding to their faith, not being magical geniuses.
chunks.text: And you see, Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, they were chosen because they stood out. They stood—they were adding to their faith. And it says in chapter 1 verse 17, you see they had knowledge, but then God gave them. Read this right here: God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom. You see, they had a level of knowledge, they had a level of wisdom, but then God came and gave them more. He added to their knowledge. I want that kind of knowledge. I want that kind of wisdom. I want that kind of understanding working in my home and my life and my family. But you see, these guys stood up for Christ. They had to begin to add faith. You have to start doing it. They stood out. They qualified. They were just qualifying. They weren’t chosen yet. They weren’t chosen yet. But God, in the middle of their qualification, from qualification to when they were chosen, God gave them more knowledge. God gave them wisdom and understanding. And it says in Daniel verse 20, in all matters of wisdom and understanding the king found them ten times better. And he found them ten times better because God gave them. God gave them knowledge. You know, they weren’t some magical awesome people. They didn’t have their own great ability. Their greatest ability was submitting to adding to their faith.

chunks.section_question: Does God meet you in the middle when you add?
chunks.short_answer: He says when you add, God meets you in the middle and gives you more—Nebuchadnezzar found them ten times better—and the New Testament says to whom who has, more will be given. You don’t have to be a genius; you choose to add.
chunks.text: And you don’t have to be a super smart person. You don’t have to be a genius. You know, I would read Daniel, I say, “Gosh, this guy, he just had so much ability.” No. He made a choice as a young person to add to his faith, to exercise what the Bible said to do. And somewhere God met him in the middle of that and gave him more knowledge, more understanding, because God did it. And you see, when you add, God is going to meet you in the middle somewhere, and he’s going to give you more. He’s going to—the Bible says in the New Testament, to whom who has, more will be given. And you see, we’ve got to add to our faith. We’ve got to discipline ourselves. And King Nebuchadnezzar found them ten times better than all in his realm.

chunks.section_question: What did God give Solomon, and did Solomon keep adding?
chunks.short_answer: From 1 Kings 4:29 he says God gave Solomon wisdom, great insight and breadth of understanding; his wisdom was greater than the men of the East and Egypt. But he notes the Bible doesn’t say Solomon was adding to his faith.
chunks.text: And we’re going to look at our second person. First Kings 4:29. God gave Solomon wisdom. You know, Solomon—I can’t see where—it doesn’t say in the Bible that he was adding to his faith. You know, I didn’t find that. So we’re going straight to the place where God gave him something. He asked for wisdom. He came to God and said, “I want wisdom to rule this people.” And it says in verse 29 that God gave Solomon wisdom, very great insight, breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand of the seashore. Solomon was given so much knowledge. He was given knowledge of things that we are finding out today in science. He was given knowledge by God that created everything. And people would come to hear all of this knowledge. Solomon’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the men of the east. I mean, how do they find this stuff out? How do they know? He was wiser than all the men of the east, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt—all the wisdom combined, it sounds like. You see, God had blessed this guy. He was wiser than any other man. But if you read in First Kings 11 verse 1 through 4, it says, “But King Solomon loved many strange women.” King Solomon started to marry. He had 700 wives and 300 concubines.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And God gave Solomon wisdom and exceedingly great understanding, and largeness of heart like the sand on the seashore.

chunks.section_question: How did Solomon fall after receiving wisdom?
chunks.short_answer: From 1 Kings 11:1-4 he says Solomon loved many strange women—700 wives and 300 concubines—and they turned his heart to idols. He threw out virtue, self-control and knowledge; God was angry and brought judgment, which matches 2 Peter’s warning.
chunks.text: He—it says the Scripture, the Bible says that his wives began to turn his heart away from God. And then we find later on that he is praising and giving thanks to another god, to an idol. And you see, Solomon, he threw out adding to his faith. He threw out virtue. You know, he wasn’t supposed to marry all those girls. That wasn’t right. He threw it out. He threw out self-control. He threw out knowledge of Christ. He threw out the Scriptures. You know, knowledge—he knew who created everything. He threw it out. He threw out virtue and godliness. And his wives turned away his heart. Later on in his life God was angry with him and brought judgment on the land. You see, in Second Peter we learned that you’re going to be blessed when you add to your faith, and if you don’t there’s going to be punishment. And that’s exactly what happened with Solomon. God gave him all this wisdom. God gave him these things. But he turned away. He left his addition.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But King Solomon loved many foreign women, as well as the daughter of Pharaoh: women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites— from the nations of whom the LORD had said to the children of Israel, “You shall not intermarry with them, nor they with you. Surely they will turn away your hearts after their gods.” Solomon clung to these in love. And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart. For it was so, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not loyal to the LORD his God, as was the heart of his father David.

chunks.section_question: What does “Daniel continued” mean for us?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Daniel 1:21 that Daniel continued into the first year of King Cyrus, and has everyone say “continued.” Daniel kept adding and became more mature; if you add to your faith you will never fall and will receive a rich welcome.
chunks.text: But it says in Daniel 1:21 that Daniel continued even into the first year of King Cyrus. Daniel continued. Everybody say “continued.” Continued. Daniel continued. He continued to add to his faith. He continued to add. He didn’t neglect. He didn’t turn his heart from God. And if you read Daniel 1 through 12, you see Daniel becoming more and more mature, more excellent, more and more. Amen. And God is showing him more and more. And he wants to show you more and more. If you do these things you will never fall. If you add to your faith you’ll never fall, and you’ll receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Thus Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus.
Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble;

faqs.question: Is believing enough, or must you do more?
faqs.answer: He says “add to your faith” means you’ve got to do more than just believe or accept Christ in your heart—you’ve got to move on.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge,

faqs.question: Can a Sunday sermon alone feed you for the week?
faqs.answer: He says Mr. [unclear] can’t fill you in 15 minutes with enough bread to last a week; you’ve got to read and study the Scriptures yourself.

faqs.question: Is controlling the tongue part of self-control?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says the Bible calls the tongue an unruly evil, and living with someone is a crash course in tongue control.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But no man can tame the tongue. It is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

faqs.question: Did Jesus love the Pharisees?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus had so much love for them that He came into conflict with them and said they were wrong, because He loved them.

faqs.question: What does “barren” mean in 2 Peter 1:8?
faqs.answer: He says barren means useless, like a cracked desert or Death Valley you can only ride on and tear up.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For if these things are yours and abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: What is a rich welcome versus a poor welcome?
faqs.answer: He contrasts a casual “yeah, you believe, come on in” with “oh, there he is, the guy who added to his faith, the guy who did—come on in.” and says he wants the rich welcome.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble;

faqs.question: Why should young people stand out?
faqs.answer: He says Daniel and his friends stood out as they added knowledge and wisdom, and that deciding as a young person to believe and add will have the best effect in your life.

scriptures.text_nkjv: young men in whom there was no blemish, but good-looking, gifted in all wisdom, possessing knowledge and quick to understand, who had ability to serve in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the language and literature of the Chaldeans.

faqs.question: Why were Daniel and his friends ten times better?
faqs.answer: He says the king found them ten times better because God gave them knowledge—not because they were magical—after they submitted to adding to their faith.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And in all matters of wisdom and understanding about which the king examined them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers who were in all his realm.

faqs.question: How many wives and concubines does he say Solomon had?
faqs.answer: He says Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines, and that his wives turned his heart away from God to an idol.

faqs.question: Will you never fall if you add to your faith?
faqs.answer: He closes with 2 Peter’s promise: if you do these things and add to your faith you will never fall, and you’ll receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus.
